name: Phishing
description: Recognize suspicious emails or messages asking for information or urgent action.
warning_signs: Unexpected requests for payment or account details|Pressure to act quickly or open an attachment
recommended_actions: Avoid replying or opening links.|Verify the request through a website or phone number you already trust.|Report the message as phishing, then delete it.
prevention_tips: Keep software updated.|Use multi-factor authentication, which adds another sign-in check.
source_name: FTC — How To Recognize and Avoid Phishing Scams

name: Weak Passwords
description: Improve short, reused, or easy-to-guess passwords that put accounts at risk.
warning_signs: The same password is used for several accounts|A password uses a common phrase or personal information
recommended_actions: Replace weak passwords with long, unique passwords.|Use a password manager to create and remember them.|Change exposed passwords and any similar passwords reused elsewhere.
prevention_tips: Turn on two-factor authentication when available.|Protect your email account because it receives password-reset links.
source_name: FTC — Creating Strong Passwords and Other Ways To Protect Your Accounts

name: Malware
description: Understand warning signs of harmful software and where to get help.
warning_signs: Unexpected redirects or unfamiliar browser add-ons|Frequent pop-ups, crashes, or unusual slowdowns; these do not prove an infection
recommended_actions: Stop entering passwords or other sensitive information on the affected device.|Update your security software and run its scan; follow its removal instructions.|If problems continue, contact a trusted support provider.|After addressing the device issue, change potentially exposed passwords and enable two-factor authentication.
prevention_tips: Keep security software updated.|Download software from its official provider, not unexpected ads.
source_name: FTC — Malware: How To Protect Against, Detect, and Remove It

name: Unsafe Links
description: Pause before following an unexpected link in an email or text message.
warning_signs: An unexpected message asks you to follow a link|The message asks for payment or personal information
recommended_actions: Do not open the suspicious link.|Reach the company through its known website or phone number.|If a download may have installed malware, update your security software and scan the device.
prevention_tips: Verify unexpected messages independently.|Keep your device software updated.
source_name: FTC — How To Recognize and Avoid Phishing Scams

name: Account Compromise
description: Respond when someone may have accessed your email or social media account.
warning_signs: A password or recovery detail changed without your action|Messages you did not send or unfamiliar sign-in notices
recommended_actions: Update your computer security software and scan for harmful software first.|If locked out, follow the account provider's official recovery instructions.|Once you regain access, change the password and sign out other devices.|Check recovery contacts and email-forwarding rules for changes you did not make.|Tell contacts to ignore suspicious messages from your account.
prevention_tips: Use a strong, unique password.|Enable two-factor authentication and keep recovery details current.
source_name: FTC — How To Recover Your Hacked Email or Social Media Account
